about.note: This is the Town of Jackson's record (Carroll County): a three-member Board of Selectmen (the town calls it the Select Board), a Town Administrator, and a traditional town meeting, with officers and zoning questions voted by ballot on the second Tuesday in March and the budget and other articles voted at a business meeting two days later. The town posts 2026 Select Board, Planning Board and other minutes as PDFs, but those files could not be opened for this research, so the newest Select Board meetings shown here are from 2025 minutes and news reports, plus one August 2026 decision documented in an official Zoning Board notice. Part of the village is served by the separate Jackson Water Precinct, which has its own tax rate. Plain-English summaries written by AI; items with needs_review=true are uncertain.

issues.title: Black Mountain ski area: site disturbance enforcement and appeal
issues.status: Zoning Board hearing on Black Mountain's appeal was rescheduled to October 30, 2026; the outcome was not yet posted
issues.summary: The Selectmen sent Black Mountain Ski Area an enforcement letter in August 2026 saying it broke the town's site disturbance rules (rules about clearing and moving earth) near Great Brook and the Wildcat River. Black Mountain appealed to the Zoning Board of Adjustment. It is the latest in a run of disputes between the town and the ski area over signs, fireworks and noise.
points: The August 12, 2026 letter, authorized at the Selectmen's August 11 meeting, cites three parts of the zoning rules: work started before a Notice of Intent was filed, work from last fall not stabilized by November 15, and no written plan before work began.
The land is Tax Map R17, Lots 28A and 31B. ZBA case 2026-02 was set for September 30, then postponed to October 30, 2026 at 7 PM.
The town has posted a timeline of the Whitneys Pond and Great Brook complaint and related Select Board minutes from July 28 and August 11, 2026.
In 2025 the ZBA upheld a town sign violation order against Black Mountain but reversed the $275 fine because the town had not given written notice first.
November 25, 2025: after a closed session on claims and litigation, the Selectmen signed a settlement agreement with Black Mountain (terms not described in the minutes).

issues.title: New fire station
issues.status: Under construction; the 2026 budget includes the first $90,000 in bond interest
issues.summary: Jackson is building a new fire station. The old station is to be used for town storage. The 2025 Town Report says the project, along with moving the Historical Society building, brought more heavy equipment into town than in many years.

issues.title: Short-term rental rules and town ordinances
issues.status: Voters approved a short-term rental zoning change 119-50 on March 10, 2026; the Selectmen keep approving and policing rental permits
issues.summary: Jackson requires a conditional use permit for each short-term rental and limits how many people can stay. Owners get a warning for a first violation, a $275 fine for a second and lose the permit on a third. In 2025 and 2026 the town rewrote its rental, parking, noise and event rules.
points: March 10, 2026: Article 2 (zoning amendment on short-term rentals) passed 119-50; the Planning Board backed it 7-0 and the Selectmen 3-0-0.
September 22, 2025: Selectmen let the Planning Board consult the town lawyer on revising the short-term rental ordinance.
October 21, 2025: Selectmen voted 3-0 to record an overcrowding incident (11 guests where 8 were allowed) without counting it as a strike.
November 25, 2025: four rental permits approved; a public hearing on a new parking ordinance for public property was set for December 9, 2025.
